The clinical picture of a 46,XX female with ambiguous genitalia (clitoromegaly/labial fusion) at birth, delayed menarche, and severe acne is classic for Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia, specifically 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency, despite the confusingly "normal" test results which may be masked by oral contraceptive use or represent a non-classic variant. The bone fragility is likely secondary to chronic androgen excess interfering with normal skeletal maturation or a concurrent issue, but the primary endocrine diagnosis fits the virilization history best.
